text: Joseph Stalin or Iosif Vissarionovich Stalin (Russian: Ио́сиф Виссарио́нович Ста́лин, pronounced [ˈjɵsʲɪf vʲɪsɐˈrʲɵnəvʲɪtɕ ˈstalʲɪn]; born Ioseb Besarionis Dze Jugashvili, Georgian: იოსებ ბესარიონის ძე ჯუღაშვილი, pronounced [iɔsɛb bɛsɑriɔnis dzɛ dʒuɣɑʃvili]; 18 December 1878[1] – 5 March 1953) was the leader of the Soviet Union from the mid-1920s until his death in 1953. Among the Bolshevik revolutionaries who took part in the Russian Revolution of 1917, Stalin was appointed general secretary of the party's Central Committee in 1922. He subsequently managed to consolidate power following the 1924 death of Vladimir Lenin through suppressing Lenin's criticisms (in the postscript of his testament) and expanding the functions of his role, all the while eliminating any opposition. He remained general secretary until the post was abolished in 1952, concurrently serving as the Premier of the Soviet Union from 1941 onward. Under Stalin's rule, the concept of "socialism in one country" became a central tenet of Soviet society. He replaced the New Economic Policy introduced by Lenin in the early 1920s with a highly centralised command economy, launching a period of industrialization and collectivization that resulted in the rapid transformation of the USSR from an agrarian society into an industrial power.[2] However, the economic changes coincided with the imprisonment of millions of people in correctional labour camps.[3] The initial upheaval in agriculture disrupted food production and contributed to the catastrophic Soviet famine of 1932–1933, known as the Holodomor in Ukraine. Between 1934 and 1939 he organized and led a massive purge (known as "Great Purge") of the party, government, armed forces and intelligentsia, in which millions of so-called "enemies of the Soviet people" were imprisoned, exiled or executed. In a period that lasted from 1936 to 1939, Stalin instituted a campaign against enemies within his regime. Major figures in the Communist Party, such as the old Bolsheviks, Leon Trotsky, and most of the Red Army generals, were killed after being convicted of plotting to overthrow the government and Stalin.[4] In August 1939, after failed attempts to conclude anti-Hitler pacts with other major European powers, Stalin entered into a non-aggression pact with Nazi Germany that divided their influence and territory within Eastern Europe, resulting in their invasion of Poland in September of that year, but Germany later violated the agreement and launched a massive invasion of the Soviet Union in June 1941. Despite heavy human and territorial losses, Soviet forces managed to halt the Nazi incursion after the decisive Battles of Moscow and Stalingrad. After defeating the Axis powers on the Eastern Front, the Red Army captured Berlin in May 1945, effectively ending the war in Europe for the Allies.[5][6] The Soviet Union subsequently emerged as one of two recognized world superpowers, the other being the United States.[7] The Yalta and Potsdam conferences established communist governments loyal to the Soviet Union in the Eastern Bloc countries as buffer states. He also fostered close relations with Mao Zedong in China and Kim Il-sung in North Korea. Stalin led the Soviet Union through its post-war reconstruction phase, which saw a significant rise in tension with the Western world that would later be known as the Cold War. During this period, the USSR became the second country in the world to successfully develop a nuclear weapon, as well as launching the Great Plan for the Transformation of Nature in response to another widespread famine and the Great Construction Projects of Communism. In the years following his death, Stalin and his regime have been condemned on numerous occasions, most notably in 1956 when his successor Nikita Khrushchev denounced his legacy and initiated a process of de-Stalinization. He remains a controversial figure today, with many regarding him as a tyrant.[8] However, popular opinion within the Russian Federation is mixed.[9][10][11] Stalin is attributed to 20,000,000–40,000,000 deaths as a result of his regime's actions.[12][13]

text: While an extreme amount of fun can be had with this game, those extreme amounts come in long intervals. The only real issue with this game is a lack of players. But if you manage to overcome this obstacle, then this game is a ton of fun. Don't expect any real twist in gameplay from Valve on this game, as it is a tribute to the glory of Quake. But this game is almost exactly that. A . If you are looking for a fun time fragging your friends like old times then this game is really only ideal if you get it in a bundle. So to paraphrase... -A remake of sorts of one of the most revolutionary FPS games of all time. A good remake at that. -Tight controls, an array of weapons, and tricks are carried over from Quake, so you will own people if you were good back in the day. -Can run on a potato and still look decent. -Can have an assortment of different pings and still play smoothly during matches. -Decent texture quality for the maps. -Good customization of your character for rounds. You can choose to play as Gman or Gordan Freeman, as well as some other characters from the original Half Life. -Good fun for you and your friends if you want an interesting "blast from the past" during a LAN party. -Comes with a few bundles so you can snag this game for next to nothing while getting some of Valve's top work. -No one plays it enough to find a lively match. -Too few servers to actually play on, but thankfully there are servers to begin with. -While the maps are mainly ports of Quake maps without their more explicit, pixel-heavy graphics, there are only around 6-8 maps total, not including Custom maps though. -Since there aren't really many matches at all, you won't really have the opportunity to enjoy this game. -Outdated gameplay mechanics by today's standards, but perfect by the logic of the original games produced by Id Software. -Weapon selection, while restricted to the original weapon selection from Quake, can become stale for more modern players. The verdict is...... Get it only in a bundle. I loved Quake, and I loved what little bit I get from this. The game offers so much, but can only really do so when you have others to play against.

text: The game had a very rough launch with bugs, Hence the low rating for the game by Meta. But those bugs are all but squashed now and the game is really solid. It's like a mix of swtor, and borderlands 2. The way the area's are created has a Swtor feel, and your running around shootings things much like Borderlands, or so I hear. (I never actually played either Borderlands, but that's how people are describing it). With only a few hours of game-play in it, I'm already getting my 10$ worth out of it easy, and the game story will draw you in. The characters personalities seem pretty solid as well, you'll hate them, love them, and get annoyed by the ones your supposed too. Ontop of that, the customization for your character is pretty legit as well, not only being able to choose which weapon and side arm you want, (which is no limitations, you could go sniper rifle/Assault Weapon Sniper Rifle/Bazooka, Pistol/Energy Gun, or even Shotgun/Shotgun) No limitations in mix and matching weapons. Just like Swtor you can break down your weapons as well for parts and income, or add accessories and mods to them which will boost their ability, as well as change your characters headgear, and outfit to mix and match. Definetly worth the 10$ easy. Cons: The few Con's I found are not huge, but could be a turn off for some players. 1) The starting area's at least are pretty empty. To me this actually enhances the feel of it being a wasteland. If there were 100's of people running around, wouldn't feel like that, so to me this is actually a plus, but for others may be a turn off. There is a helpful automatic party finder however, which helps to get groups. 2) The Chat system is totally implimented bad. You can never see what anyone is saying around you or in the area. To see it, you have to stop what your doing and press Enter. Which then a Chat screen the size of the entire screen pops up. Which only then can you respond. Terrible chat system for an action game, because half way through responding to what your friend just said your getting shot at, and need to stop. However if you use VOIP to talk with friends, again, the chat system is of no concern for you really.

title: democracy 3
text: Excellent politics simulator, where you quickly realize that trying to save the economy (too fast at least) will not make you succeed. I find myself coming back to this again and again. You have to have some level of interest towards simulations or how different things depend on each other or politics in general to enjoy this. Pros: -Lot of options to tune your policies -Country differences -Updates have been made, which keeps the content more current. Also moddable, although did not play those yet. Cons: -Quite simplistic UI, which focuses on the policies dependencies - it does its job, but is not very flashy -Some level of repetitiveness -Would be nice to have some "party program" aspect in the game, i.e. what did you promise in your campaing etc. Other: -If you have the mindset of fix economy, you will face consequences pretty fast usually...

title: democracy 3
text: I enjoyed the game for the most part, it's not a bad game, only voting negative to emphasise certain problems. There are hard limits on how high or low you can get every stat. It's kind of lame to be unable to be that extra bit of productivity or technology, but it's even more lame when your private healthcare is capped out (or just plain not supplying enough) because you took away public healthcare. This is also part of an overall trend you will find in this game. Smaller government simply isn't a viable strategy. The game is designed so that more government policies is the solution to everything. The benefits to lowering taxes are negligable, and no one really cares that much if you increase it. There is a bit of a laffer curve, but it's evidently too far to the right. Putting money in the hands of rich people, or really any class of people just doesn't seem to do all that much either. Increasing the size of the police and research teams is pretty much always a good choice. Things like govenment corruption in research doesn't exist, and I feel should be a much, much bigger problem for big government. Also having all these government beaurocrats doesn't create any "burdensome regulations" affecting buisness, which is very unrealistic. There's also no inflation. I'll be a bit less critical for this next point, as meeting this one would be above and beyond what I'd have expected, but this game is a bit too materialistic. I think it missed an opportunity to focus on other things than just money, happiness and votes. Things like religiousity, beauty, and national pride. Now they do actually have things like religious voter happiness, tourism, and patriotism, which do technically suggest these things, but I feel they could have taken it a step further and make it more of an end in it of itself instead of just a means to more happiness, money and votes. I recognise that politics does tend to have a bit of cynicism associated with it, but that doesn't mean you shouldn't be able to have higher pursuits. Another thing is that you're essentailly competing against yourself. It isn't terrible, it's just that it'd be cool if say you were competing with france for tourists, or china for manufactoring jobs, ya know? There's also no growth rate, and therefore no policies that affect growth rate, which would have been nice touch. Immigration is too hard to curb once you're doing amazing, which is silly because it's very possible to defend a boarder from most immigration, just take a look at the effectiveness of isreal's boarder barrier. I'd say overall this game does have a bit of a normie bias (center/left, big government), and doesn't really allow or work for any of the more interesting experimental governments that have/haven't been tried yet like republicanism, snekonomics or anarchy. You can be socialist, and have a big military, so I guess that's close enough to nazism, although you can't make it into a dictatorship, though there is survelance state which I guess is close enough. Appearantly you can actually achieve "real communism" because communist policies actually work in this game, which realistically they really shouldn't, (although I'd say still allow it too for the fun of it... even though I hate communism). Really I just feel they needed to explore more different types of governments and make right wing / anarchist playstyles more viable, and especially, big government and liberal policies need to have more intrinsic consequences other than♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off conservatives.

title: democracy 3
text: This game is fun and engaging, and actually does a lot to deepen your practical understanding of how politics work. Not necessarily regarding specifics (not every country is willing to even discuss having creationism taught in its schools, dear game), but more generally. It really lets you experience the frustration and practical necessity of tradeoffs you have to make if you want to sign a policy you care about into law, but also be re-elected, not f*ck up the economy, and keep the rich taxpayers and skilled workers from emigrating to other countries... All this happens without finger-wagging, however. It's a fun, engaging game and you sort of learn a lot by pleasant accident.  I recommend this game to just about everyone. If you don't care about politics, it's perfect for you. If you do care about politics, it's also perfect for you. Go play it.

text: This is one of the best games I have ever played.  Normally I prefer FPS or Strategy so Democracy 3 was a leap for me, but boy am I happy I have.  Democracy 3 is simple to learn, but delightfully complex.  This is the only game my wife and I play together (sometimes until 3 am...), and it's fun to see how different policy changes ripple back through the system.  I try to get all my friends and coworkers to play as well.  It's a fun game, I strongly recommend it, and make sure you check out the mods as well.
